corpus.evidence: no vulnerable/safe corpus authored beside this record; fixtures live in the plugin's own tests.

oracle.evidence: no independent decider. SonarQube computes the same metric and is the obvious one.
oracle.command: score findings against sonarjs on the same corpus

effectiveFp.evidence: not measured under the formal protocol. One class is now out of scope by construction: 32% of corpus findings were in machine-generated files, where nobody reads the advice. 671 -> 227. What remains has not been sampled.

reachability.evidence: not applicable in the taint sense — this is a structural metric, not a source-to-sink question.

duel.evidence: not scored against sonarjs, the direct competitor for this metric.

adversarial.evidence: no wave written against this rule. On the two maintainability rules where one was written it found a real defect in each, so absence of evidence is not evidence here.

realSource.evidence: 8 pinned repositories, measured against the LOCAL tree (before #612 the rig ran local plugins against the published devkit). 671 -> 227.

partition.evidence: probed against the other two maintainability rules that visit the same function nodes. The corpus splits cleanly: identical-functions 258, cognitive-complexity 227, max-parameters 74, none subsuming another.

coverage.evidence: 100% statements / branches / functions / lines across eslint-plugin-maintainability, 405 tests.

knownGaps.summary: the rule does not look at files that declare themselves machine-generated.
knownGaps.why: maintainability advice is addressed to whoever edits the file next, and generated code has no such reader — the next generator run rewrites it wholesale, and twilio-node's header says "Do not edit the class manually" outright. Decided by the file's OWN declaration (an @generated docblock or a "this code was generated by" banner in the LEADING comments), never by whether the path contains the word.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a generated file is found that carries no banner and the class is large enough to matter.

knownGaps.summary: test files are NOT skipped, unlike identical-functions.
knownGaps.why: deliberate, and the rule-creator records the reasoning: a convoluted test is still a readability cost to whoever debugs it when it fails, so complexity advice applies there in a way duplication advice does not. Duplication in a test IS the test; complexity in a test is not.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: an effectiveFp sample shows test-file findings of this rule going unactioned at the same rate as the generated ones did.

notes: Seal record OPENED 2026-08-22, alongside the change that added skipGeneratedFiles. The generated share was PREDICTED from the corpus at 32% before the change and the change removed exactly 32%, which is the evidence that the predicate silenced the generated set and nothing else.
